processing: Fully oxidised black tea made as orthodox leaf, including tippy golden grades, and as CTC.
harvest_season: The May to June second flush is the prized picking, valued for its chunky golden tips.
appearance_dry: Dark leaf with an unusually high share of chunky golden tips in second-flush lots.
appearance_liquor: Coppery red to deep brown, by its seller's description.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown leaf with lighter tips.
taste_profile: Full-bodied and malty with some spice and an earthy, almost stout-like depth and a firm astringency.

brewing.notes: Drink it hot. It stands up to milk, but try a tippy lot plain first.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush; second-flush lots from May and June are the ones to look for, and CTC is sold as an everyday line. Like other Assam teas, it tastes best within a year or two of picking.
description:
Khongea is a family-run garden in Upper Assam, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Its reputation rests on second-flush tea with an unusual amount of chunky golden tip.

It makes both tippy orthodox leaf and CTC. The orthodox grades carry the golden buds that shape a rounder cup, and the CTC is built for strength and speed.

The second-flush cup is broad and malty with some spice and an earthy, stout-beer depth, and it has enough grip to take milk. Keep it hot, and watch the steep length, since a long steep turns the astringency hard.

Check the flush on the label and look for visible tip in the dry leaf. Golden Tips and CTC are very different purchases under the same garden name.
history: Accounts of the garden's age disagree. Its seller copy says it was established in the late nineteenth century by two English women planters, a claim not confirmed independently. A travel guide says it came into existence around 1949, but the same seller says 1949 is when it came to the Prakash family, who still own and manage it.
